newsitem.title: japan: TIFFE Euroyen ends higher on soaring JGBs.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen ends higher on soaring JGBs.

text.p: The key June three-month Euroyen deposit rate contract ended higher on TIFFE on Wednesday in response to soaring Japanese government bonds (JGBs) in both cash and futures markets, traders said.

The bullish market experienced only a temporary set-back after a news agency report quoting an Liberal Democratic Party official as saying the Bank of Japan should raise its discount rate to the one percent level from the current 0.5.

"The market did not take it (the LDP official's remark) seriously amid a widely held belief that the BOJ will not be able to make changes in its monetary policy before the middle of next year," a city bank trader said.
In response to this growing market perception, turnover in the September contract has been quickly catching up with that of the June.

In the cash market, the key three-month certificates of deposit were traded at 0.51-0.52 percent, compared with Tuesday's 0.51 percent. However, traders called the slight firming in the CD rate purely technical.

The three-month CD rate of 0.51 percent reflected market expectations that commercial banks will be able to cover the seasonal fund shortfall at the end of the year without much difficulty, traders said.
The key overnight call rate was most heavily traded at 0.49 percent, unchanged from Tuesday.
The two-year interest rate swap rate was quoted at 0.87-0.91 percent, down from Tuesday's 0.92-0.96 percent.
